title: Pointwise differential criterion for smoothness
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $x\in X$, let $s=f(x)$, and put $d=\dim_x(X_s)$ for the dimension at $x$ [def-kun-dimension] of the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Say that $f$ is smooth at $x$ if there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $f|_U:U\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $f$ is smooth at $x$ if and only if the local ring map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $\Omega^1_{X/S,x}$, the stalk of the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], can be generated by at most $d$ elements.

source.place: Tag 01V9 (morphisms-lemma-smooth-at-point), equivalence of (1) and (3); 'smooth at x' as in Morphisms Definition 01V5

proof.text: Suppose f is smooth on U containing x. Use the proved source-library Smooth.exists_smoothOfRelativeDimension_resLE on U→S (the standard-smooth affine chart argument) to find a smaller open source of relative dimension d. Its composite open immersion j into X identifies it with O=j.opensRange. Transport across j.isoOpensRange to obtain SmoothOfRelativeDimension d for O→S. Smoothness gives flatness of the stalk map of U→S, and cancel the isomorphism induced by U→X to obtain flatness of f.stalkMap x.

Apply lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free to O→S. Choose a local trivialization of rank d around x. Taking germs of its finite frame gives a basis of its differential stalk; the already proved source-library exists_basis_stalk_of_over_iso_free implements this coordinate-germ argument. The relativeDifferentialsRestrictIso and additive restriction-stalk isomorphism identify this with the stalk for f. The scalar compatibility is lem-pc-restrict-stalk-inv-smul, inverted using bijectivity. Map the d basis vectors across this semilinear equivalence: span induction, using its addition and scalar formulas, proves that they span the ambient stalk. This includes d=0.

Let B be the inverse image of O in X_{f(x)}. Paste the restriction pullback with the defining fibre square. The map B→Spec κ(f(x)) is smooth of relative dimension d by base change. The proved topologicalKrullDimAt_eq_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension gives dimension d at the marked point of B. IsOpen.topologicalKrullDimAt_eq gives the same dimension at f.asFiber x. Thus the d stalk generators satisfy the required bound.

Conversely obtain W,V,q, the finite presentation, flatness equivalence and generator equivalence from lem-trf-affine-chart-stalk-differentials. Equip R=Γ(S,V) and A=Γ(X,W) with the algebra structure of f.appLE. The chart point equalities and SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec give precisely the inputs of lem-trf-affine-fibre-point-dimension. Its prime Q contracts to q; injectivity of the inverse of PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber identifies Q with the canonical kernel prime used by the ring criteria. Its finite-type conclusion and dimension equality identify the affine fibre dimension with dim at f.asFiber x.

Transfer the given n generators to the localized differential module using the chart equivalence. Apply lem-trf-fibre-cotangent-localization-generators. Its comparison theorem gives finrank at most n for Ω_{F/κ(p)} tensor_F κ(Q), with its specified transported κ(Q)-module structure. Tensor commutativity, viewed as a linear equivalence for precisely that transported action, changes this to κ(Q) tensor_F Ω_{F/κ(p)} without changing finrank. Cast the natural-number inequality into WithBot ℕ∞ and combine it with the assumed n bound and the affine-fibre dimension equality.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-differentials-dimension-bound-smooth-at-prime at the canonical prime of the affine fibre. Then apply lem-weil-pbc-flat-smooth-fibre-smooth-at-prime to R→A, using the stalk flatness equivalence. Its finite-presentation witness is g=1: localization away from one is finitely presented over A, and finite presentation is transitive. This proves Algebra.IsSmoothAtPrime R q.

Unpack Algebra.IsSmoothAtPrime into g outside q and a smooth R-algebra A_g. Mathlib basicOpen_subset_smoothLocus_iff_smooth places q in Algebra.smoothLocus R A. Mathlib formallySmooth_stalkMap_iff transports this to formal smoothness of the actual stalk map. Finally take f.smoothLocus: its preimage under its open inclusion is the top open, by preimage_smoothLocus_eq. The equivalence smoothLocus_eq_top_iff gives smoothness of its restriction, so this is the required neighbourhood.

lean.statement: theorem smoothAtPoint_iff_flat_stalkMap_and_differentials_generators {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) : (∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ f)) ↔ (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj f.relativeDifferentials), (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber x) ∧ Submodule.span (X.presheaf.stalk x) (Set.range v) = ⊤

reviewed_lean.note: The statement matches node and Stacks 01V9 (1)<=>(3) clause by clause. [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]; smooth at x = ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ f), target S, the node's own definition; (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat; relative differential stalk through RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor of f.relativeDifferentials; ∃ n : ℕ, Fin n spanning family over X.presheaf.stalk x with n ≤ topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber x), i.e. dim_x of the scheme fibre, not the local ring.
